answer: Diminishing Anchor Credits: each agent action draws from a per-identity credit anchor that halves on every independent corroboration, so identities prove value only through costly, verifiable lineage. Attackers minting N sybils face marginal cost rising as ~c·N²: the ivory of fresh identities yields near-zero credits until each is anchored by paid attestations, and the canyon between cheap first action and expensive sustained participation widens geometrically. Cost: forging K credible identities scales quadratically, making majority capture economically irrational.
